description:
FILED s538 (reviewing session, 2026-11-10) from the review probes of s536j (PPI batch 8, #4542 group AW).  PRE-EXISTING: main 4a39a1c7 and the s536j tree 094108ec answer the same on every line below; the batch fixed the STATEMENT-START shapes (`x3();`, `x3;`) and regressed nothing (probes ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s538/review/j/p2.pl, q1..q13.pl).

REPRODUCERS (perl 5.40.3), one per file:

    sub x64 { "x64" } print x64(), "\n";          # perl x64    PCL: statement dropped (loud), dies at the site
    sub x3 { 7 } print x3() x2, "\n";             # perl 77     PCL: statement dropped (loud)
    sub x3 { "X3" } print STDOUT x3(), "\n";      # perl X3     PCL: prints NOTHING, exit 0  -- SILENT WRONG

RIGHT today (controls): `my $v = x3();`, `(x3(), x3())`, `"a" . x3()`, `P->x3`, `$h{x3}`, `("a") x3`, `"q" x3`, and a sub named plain `x` in the print slot (`print x(), "\n"`).

PPI tokens (vendored, branch pcl c2f21706 and a376a6d8 alike):
    print x64(), "\n";        ->  Word<print> Operator<x> Number<64> ( ) , ...
    print STDOUT x3(), "\n";  ->  Word<print> Word<STDOUT> Operator<x> Number<3> ( ) , ...
    print x(), "\n";          ->  Word<print> Operator<x> ( ) , ...      (the same mis-lex; a PCL repair or PExpr covers the digit-less name)
  expected: Word<x64> / Word<x3>: after a list operator (and after its filehandle) perl expects a TERM, so `x` cannot be the repetition operator there (toke.c: PL_expect == XTERM / XREF).

Owner: the next PPI batch (vendor/PPI branch `pcl`, two-commit PR shape, rows in docs/ppi-bug-report.t + t/ppi_bugs_pcl.t, catalogue section beside the 19 / 19b / 63 family, registry row in Pl/PPIBugs.pm).  The fix site is the same expect question group AW answered for the statement start: is an OPERATOR legal here?  After a Word that is a list operator (print / say / printf / return / push ..., or any Word that is not a term end) and after a print filehandle the answer is no.  Probe the breaking shapes: `print $x x3`, `print "a" x3`, `print FH x3` where no sub x3 exists (perl: a string repetition of the bareword?  measure), `return x3()`, `push @a, x3()`, `print {$fh} x3()`.
subject: PPI: a sub named x<N> (x3, x64) in a LIST-OPERATOR argument slot -- `print x64()`, `print STDOUT x3()`, `print x3() x2` -- is lexed as the operator `x` + a Number; two shapes drop the statement, `print STDOUT x3()` prints NOTHING silently (#4542 residue)
